servlet is the JAX-WS RI's HTTP-servlet transport (WSServlet, WSServletContextListener, ServletAdapter, etc.). Resolving testImplementation com.sun.xml.ws:servlet:4.0.5 already transitively pulls in jakarta.servlet:jakarta.servlet-api:6.1.0 (compile-scope dependency of the artifact itself) and jakarta.jws.WebService/WebMethod/... annotations (bundled inside the transitively-pulled jakarta.xml.ws-api:4.0.3), so both the Servlet API and the JAX-WS annotations needed to write and deploy a test endpoint are already on the test classpath with no extra coordinates. This repo's existing precedent for servlet-API-consuming libraries (e.g. org.apache.commons:commons-fileupload2-javax) is to hand-write fake ServletContext/HttpServletRequest/HttpServletResponse implementations directly in the test rather than adding Mockito or a container; the same approach applies here. library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Write plain JUnit tests that exercise the reachable classes directly (ServletAdapterList, HttpSessionScopeFeature/HttpSessionInstanceResolver, WSServletDelegate, ServletConnectionImpl, WSServletContextListener) rather than depending on a live servlet container. Where a ServletContext/HttpServletRequest/HttpServletResponse is needed, hand-implement the interface (see tests/src/org.apache.commons/commons-fileupload2-javax/*/src/test/java/.../Commons_fileupload2_javaxTest.java for the established in-repo pattern) instead of adding a mocking library. To exercise WSServletContextListener's endpoint deployment path, a minimal test service class annotated with jakarta.jws.WebService plus an in-memory sun-jaxws.xml descriptor (served via the fake ServletContext's getResourceAsStream) is sufficient — no extra dependency is required since jakarta.jws annotations ship inside jakarta.xml.ws-api, already transitive. No special environment variables or system properties are documented as required by JAX-WS RI's servlet transport for standalone use.
risks: If the generated tests attempt full end-to-end SOAP request dispatch (building a real SOAP envelope and asserting a response body), that pulls in more of the jaxws-rt runtime (already covered by the existing com.sun.xml.ws:jaxws-rt:4.0.5 metadata) and increases test complexity, but does not require new setup.

The servlet module registers a jakarta.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer (META-INF/services) and pulls in JMX-related transitive deps (org.glassfish.gmbal, management-api) for monitoring probes; these should initialize harmlessly in a plain JVM test but are worth watching if native-image agent tracing surfaces unexpected JMX/ASM reflection during generateMetadata.
